generation.generator: one-off inline Python; no runtime harness mutation or random values
generation.method: Deterministic NBT construction with Python nbtlib 2.0.4; gzip-compressed big-endian NBT; fixed metadata timestamps; palette indices packed contiguously, least-significant bits first, two bits per entry.

independentOracleRelativeToOrigin.acceptanceNote: Must begin with a naturally occurring occupied block and end AIR.

placement.originRule: Read and pin the numeric active Litematica placement origin before issuing @build; it is the rotation anchor. For this fixture only, the authored Z extent is zero and CLOCKWISE_90 maps (x,y,0) to (0,y,x), so the anchor also equals the transformed bounding-box minimum. All oracle coordinates are relative to that origin; add O componentwise. Do not infer the origin from the adapter snapshot under test.
placement.transform: Litematica 0.28.8 PositionUtils.getTransformedBlockPos applies CLOCKWISE_90 as (-z,y,x). For each authored global coordinate (x,y,z) in this fixture and placement origin O=(Ox,Oy,Oz), expected world coordinate is O+(-z,y,x); because all authored z coordinates are 0, offsets are (0,y,x). The transformed X minimum is 0, so no translation is required. +X maps to +Z.

verification.independentDecode: After writing, reopen with nbtlib (separate pass) and independently decode all palette/index cells, NBT metadata and chest payload; verify SHA-256.
verification.loaderAcceptance: UNVERIFIED: actual Litematica native loader acceptance, active placement transform, and state transform require root to package/run the candidate in Minecraft 26.2. This artifact generation is not gameplay evidence.
verification.rotationOracleEvidence: Installed run/mods/litematica-fabric-26.2-0.28.8.jar inspected with javap -p -c: PositionUtils.getTransformedBlockPos switch case 1 constructs BlockPos(-z,y,x); Rotation.CLOCKWISE_90 maps to switch case 1. This corrects the original erroneous coordinate formula, which mapped +X to -Z.
